To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vector boson production with jets, including the heavy flavour production, has been measured at Tevatron and LHC.
the cross sections of vector boson production with heavy and light flavour jets are measured with high accuracy, and the measurements agree with theoretical calculations.
the cross section for vector boson production with heavy-flavor jets is measured at both the Tevatron and the LHC, and is consistent with NLO calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: - Measurements on vector bosons produced in association with light jets, charm and bottom quarks at the Tevatton and the LHC - Measurements on vector mesons produced in association light jets at the LHC - Studies on the background from vector boson+jet production in top quark pair analyses at the Tevaton and LHC - Studies of the systematic uncertainties in top quark cross section and mass measurements at the Tevatorn and LHC
the measurement of the cross section for the production of vector bosons (W or Z) in association with jets, with the focus on jets containing heavy flavour quarks.
measurements of the production of W and Z bosons with associated jets, and with the use of these measurements to estimate background in top quark studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the vector boson+jet production is well understood in the light jet case and in the case of top quark production, but that the heavy flavour production is not well described by the current theoretical predictions.
the vector boson + jet background is well understood, but not fully understood.
the vector boson + jets background has to be treated with great care in top quark cross-section measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have studied a number of systematic uncertainties in top quark cross section measurements.
vector boson production with jets is a well understood process, with the exception of the W+jets production in association with b-jets.
the vector boson production is well understood in the light jet region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theoretical predictions are not sufficiently precise to allow for a precise extraction of the top quark mass.
the theoretical uncertainty on the vector boson+heavy flavour jet cross section is large, and the theoretical uncertainties on vector boson+light jet cross sections are not yet under control.

, while the theoretical uncertainties on the vector boson+light flavour jet background are under control, there are still large uncertainties on the vector+heavy flavour background, especially for the W+b-jet and Z+b-jet backgrounds.
